extracted.intended_audience: researchers and grant-writers preparing applications to the Wellcome Trust (UK and global health research applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for preparing competitive grant applications to Wellcome Trust funding schemes, including Early-Career, Career Development, Discovery and specific accelerator calls; covers priorities, eligibility, reviewer expectations and application process practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with Wellcome funding priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Research should fit Wellcome's strategic priority areas: Discovery research into life, health and wellbeing; Mental health (anxiety, depression, psychosis broadly defined); Infectious diseases and global health challenges; Climate and health impacts; research spanning physical sciences, social sciences, clinical research, arts and humanities; and Global South research leadership and capacity building.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly demonstrate how the proposed work addresses one or more of these priority areas and the funder's stated focus on global health equity and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation / transformative potential
rubrics_metrics.description: "Demonstrate how work goes beyond incremental progress to offer genuinely new approaches"—applications must show the project is a new direction that goes beyond the 'same-old' in the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasise transformative potential rather than safe, predictable outcomes; highlight novelty in aims, concepts, methods, or expected impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant positioning / unique expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: "Show why you're uniquely qualified to deliver the proposed research"—applicants must explain their unique capabilities and why they are the right person/team to carry out the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence of track record, prior relevant work, complementary skills within the team, and a clear statement of the applicant's intellectual leadership and role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research environment and institutional support
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers look for a strong institutional environment: appropriate facilities, identified mentors/collaborators, and clear institutional backing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document institutional resources, letters/support from host organisation, named collaborators/mentors, and how the environment will enable project success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk appetite and support for calculated risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Wellcome supports calculated risks and innovative research approaches—applications that are ambitious but plausible are favoured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articulate the uncertainties, mitigations, and why the potential benefits justify the risks; avoid being overly conservative in framing the research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five-year focus and realistic near-term planning
rubrics_metrics.description: "Reviewers concentrate on first five years - pitch detail accordingly"—proposals should prioritise and detail achievable objectives within an initial five-year horizon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure aims, milestones and resources around a clear five-year plan; longer-term visions can be noted but reviewers expect concrete near-term deliverables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstration of leadership and intellectual ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications should "show intellectual ownership and project development capability"—evidence of leadership potential and capacity to drive the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show prior leadership roles, evidence of independent thinking, plans for project management and development, and how the applicant will steer the research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global impact and equity focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate how research addresses urgent health challenges affecting everyone, with attention to global health equity and capacity-building in the Global South where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain potential for population-level or systems impact, relevance to underserved settings, and concrete plans for equitable research partnerships or capacity strengthening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit to scheme-specific eligibility and budget rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Different schemes have explicit budget, duration and eligibility constraints (e.g., Early-Career Awards: up to £400,000 research expenses plus salary (5 years); Career Development Awards: usually below £250,000 per year excluding salary (8 years); Discovery Awards: no maximum budget limit (8 years)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the correct funding scheme and ensure the proposal adheres to that scheme's duration, budget limits, and eligibility requirements; consult scheme-specific guidance pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible research areas / exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Wellcome does not fund certain work: large clinical trials for drug/product development primarily for diagnosis or treatment; clinical service provision or reorganisation; animal disease studies not transmissible to humans or modelling human biology; research solely for public engagement; and mental health research outside their stated focus areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check exclusions before applying; if your project touches excluded areas, either reframe to fit Wellcome priorities or apply elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission and institutional approval requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be submitted through the Wellcome Funding Platform and require institution approval 5 working days before the deadline; there are fixed deadlines (not rolling).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure institutional approvals are obtained in time and follow the platform's submission process exactly to avoid administrative disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation time and iterative review
rubrics_metrics.description: "Allow plenty of time ahead of the deadline - avoid rushing your application" and "get as much advice as you can - ask others to share successful and unsuccessful applications."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start months in advance, conduct multiple internal and external reviews, use sample successful/unsuccessful applications as models, and incorporate feedback from diverse reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of institutional pre-application support
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-application support is available through institutional research offices and applicants are advised to contact research support early.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage your research office for budgeting, compliance, and institutional endorsement; leverage internal peer-review and administrative guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reapplication policy and expectations for resubmissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Unsuccessful applicants can submit one more application for the same project, but the second application must include substantial modifications; there is no waiting period or prior approval required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When resubmitting, address committee feedback explicitly and make significant changes rather than minor edits to improve chances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicit diverse feedback including from different fields and past applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: "Seek feedback from colleagues inside and outside your field, including successful and unsuccessful applicants" to strengthen applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate perspectives from disciplinary and non-disciplinary reviewers to catch assumptions, improve clarity, and better articulate significance and feasibility.
